events.text: Roman Emperor Valentinian I learns the Alemanni have crossed the Rhine and invaded Gaul.
Emperor Otto III issues a deed to Gottschalk, Bishop of Freising, which is the oldest known document using the name Ostarrîchi (Austria in Old High German).
After Empress Matilda released her rival King Stephen, he in turn released Robert of Gloucester, her strongest supporter, thus prolonging the Anglo-Norman civil war known as The Anarchy.

main.desc: Holy Roman Empress from 1114 to 1125; claimant to the English throne

events.text: Empress Matilda's reign as "Lady of the English" ends as Stephen of Blois regains the title of "King of England".

main.desc: Holy Roman Empress from 1114 to 1125; claimant to the English throne

events.text: Philip II is crowned King of France.
Byzantine–Seljuk wars: Seljuq Turks captured the important port city of Sinope.

main.desc: Series of conflicts in the Middle Ages

events.text: The port city of Sinope surrenders to the Seljuq Turks.

main.desc: Municipality in Turkey on the Black Sea

events.text: The anti-royalist Union of Valencia attacks the Jews of Murviedro on the pretext that they are serfs of the King of Valencia and thus "royalists".

main.desc: Anti-royalist movement in the Kingdom of Valencia from 1283 to the 15th century

events.text: Cardinal Giuliano della Rovere is elected Pope and takes the name Julius II.
The ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, painted by Michelangelo, is exhibited to the public for the first time.

main.desc: Chapel in the Apostolic Palace, Vatican City

events.text: The Strait of Magellan, the passage immediately south of mainland South America connecting the Pacific and the Atlantic Oceans, is first discovered and navigated by European explorer Ferdinand Magellan during the first recorded circumnavigation voyage.

main.desc: Strait in southern Chile between the Atlantic and Pacific

events.text: French Huguenots establish the France Antarctique colony in present-day Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.

main.desc: Historical religious group of French Protestants

events.text: The All Saints' Flood devastates the Dutch coast.

main.desc: Flooding on the coasts of Germany and the Netherlands

events.text: During the Time of Troubles, Polish troops are expelled from Moscow's Kitay-gorod by Russian troops under the command of Dmitry Pozharsky (22 October O.S.).

links.t: Old Style and New Style dates

events.text: The British Crown colony of New York is subdivided into 12 counties.

links.t: List of counties in New York

events.text: William III of Orange sets out a second time from Hellevoetsluis in the Netherlands to seize the crowns of England, Scotland and Ireland from King James II of England during the Glorious Revolution.

main.desc: King of England, Scotland, and Ireland from 1689 to 1702

events.text: In Portugal, Lisbon is totally devastated by a massive earthquake and tsunami, killing an estimated 40,000 to 60,000 people.

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Portugal

events.text: The British Parliament enacts the Stamp Act on the Thirteen Colonies in order to help pay for British military operations in North America.
Edmund Burke publishes Reflections on the Revolution in France, in which he predicts that the French Revolution will end in a disaster.

links.t: Reflections on the Revolution in France

events.text: John Adams becomes the first President of the United States to live in the Executive Mansion (later renamed the White House).

main.desc: President of the United States from 1797 to 1801

events.text: Napoleon Bonaparte invades Austria during the War of the Third Coalition.
Congress of Vienna opens to re-draw the European political map after the defeat of France in the Napoleonic Wars.

main.desc: 1814–1815 meetings to create a peace plan for Europe

events.text: The disposable ship Columbus (pictured) arrived in the The Downs off England, becoming, at that time, the largest vessel to have crossed the Atlantic Ocean.

main.desc: Ship or sea vessel intended for use on a single voyage

events.text: In Boston, Massachusetts, the first medical school for women, Boston Female Medical School (which later merged with the Boston University School of Medicine), opens.

main.desc: Capital and largest city in Massachusetts, United States

events.text: American Civil War: U.S. President Abraham Lincoln appoints George B. McClellan as the commander of the Union Army, replacing General Winfield Scott.
In the United States, the Weather Bureau (later renamed the National Weather Service) makes its first official meteorological forecast.

main.desc: U.S. forecasting agency of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration

events.text: The Battle of Bembezi took place and was the most decisive battle won by the British in the First Matabele War of 1893.

main.desc: 1893 battle of the First Matabele War

links.t: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

events.text: Nicholas II becomes the new (and last) Tsar of Russia after his father, Alexander III, dies.
Buffalo Bill, 15 of his Native Americans, and Annie Oakley were filmed by Thomas Edison in his Black Maria Studio in West Orange, New Jersey.
A picture showing the bare breasts of a woman appears in National Geographic magazine for the first time.
The first Library of Congress building opens its doors to the public; the library had previously been housed in the Congressional Reading Room in the U.S. Capitol.
Italian Sport-Club Juventus is founded by a group of students of Liceo Classico Massimo d'Azeglio.

main.desc: Association football club in Turin, Italy

events.text: Lahti, a city in Finland, is granted city rights by Tsar Nicholas II of Russia, the last Grand Duke of Finland.
World's first combat aerial bombing mission takes place in Libya during the Italo-Turkish War. Second Lieutenant Giulio Gavotti of Italy drops several small bombs.

main.desc: 1911–1912 war in Libya and the Aegean Sea

events.text: World War I: The first contingent of the First Australian Imperial Force departed Albany, Western Australia.

World War I: The first British Royal Navy defeat of the war with Germany, the Battle of Coronel, is fought off of the western coast of Chile, in the Pacific, with the loss of HMS Good Hope and HMS Monmouth.
World War I: The Australian Imperial Force (AIF) departed by ship in a single convoy from Albany, Western Australia bound for Egypt.

main.desc: Expeditionary force during World War I

events.text: In Russia, Pavel Milyukov delivers in the State Duma the famous "stupidity or treason" speech, precipitating the downfall of the government of Boris Stürmer.

World War I: With a brave action carried out into the waters of the Austro-Hungarian port of Pula, two officers of the Italian Regia Marina sink with a manned torpedo the enemy battleship SMS Viribus Unitis.
Malbone Street wreck: The worst rapid transit accident in US history occurs under the intersection of Malbone Street and Flatbush Avenue, Brooklyn, New York City, with at least 102 deaths.
Western Ukraine separates from Austria-Hungary.
Frances Kyle was called to the Bar of Ireland, becoming the first female barrister in Ireland or Great Britain.
Abolition of the Ottoman sultanate: The last sultan of the Ottoman Empire, Mehmed VI, abdicates.

main.desc: Abolition of the monarchy in Turkey

events.text: The Finnish airline Aero O/Y (now Finnair) is founded.
The Law on the Adoption and Implementation of the Turkish Alphabet, replaces the Arabic alphabet with the Latin alphabet.

main.desc: Latin script for the Turkish language

events.text: Stalinists execute Pastor Paul Hamberg and seven members of Azerbaijan's Lutheran community.

main.desc: Political and economic policies implemented by Joseph Stalin

events.text: Seabiscuit defeats War Admiral in an upset victory during a match race deemed "the match of the century" in horse racing.
American photographer Ansel Adams (pictured) shot Moonrise, Hernandez, New Mexico, one of his most famous photographs.
American photographer Ansel Adams takes a picture of a moonrise over the town of Hernandez, New Mexico that would become one of the most famous images in the history of photography.
World War II: Matanikau Offensive begins during the Guadalcanal campaign and ends three days later with an American victory.

World War II: The 3rd Marine Division, United States Marines, landing on Bougainville in the Solomon Islands, secures a beachhead, leading that night to a naval clash at the Battle of Empress Augusta Bay.
World War II: An American F-13 Superfortress made the first flight by an Allied aircraft over Tokyo since the Doolittle Raid in April 1942.
World War II: Units of the British Army land at Walcheren.

main.desc: 1944 battle on the Western Front of World War II

events.text: The official North Korean newspaper, Rodong Sinmun, is first published under the name Chongro.
Athenagoras I, Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople, is enthroned.

main.desc: Ecumenical Patriarch of Constantinople from 1948 to 1972

events.text: All 55 people on board Eastern Air Lines Flight 537 are killed when the Douglas DC-4 operating the flight collides in mid-air with a Bolivian Air Force Lockheed P-38 Lightning aircraft over Alexandria, Virginia.
Puerto Rican nationalists Griselio Torresola and Oscar Collazo attempt to assassinate US President Harry S. Truman at Blair House.

links.t: Attempted assassination of Harry S. Truman

events.text: Operation Buster–Jangle: Six thousand five hundred United States Army soldiers are exposed to 'Desert Rock' atomic explosions for training purposes in Nevada. Participation is not voluntary.
Nuclear weapons testing: The United States successfully detonates Ivy Mike, the first thermonuclear device, at the Eniwetok atoll. The explosion had a yield of ten megatons TNT equivalent.

main.desc: Controlled detonation of nuclear weapons for scientific or political purposes

events.text: The Front de Libération Nationale fires the first shots of the Algerian War of Independence.
The establishment of a Military Assistance Advisory Group in South Vietnam marks the beginning of American involvement in the conflict.

main.desc: US military advisors sent to other countries to help train their armed forces

events.text: The bombing of United Air Lines Flight 629 occurs near Longmont, Colorado, killing all 39 passengers and five crew members aboard the Douglas DC-6B airliner.

main.desc: Flight that exploded over Longmont, Colorado in November 1955

events.text: The Indian states Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka were formally created under the States Reorganisation Act.

The Indian states Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, and Mysore are formally created under the States Reorganisation Act; Kanyakumari district is joined to Tamil Nadu from Kerala. Delhi was established as a union territory.

Hungarian Revolution: Imre Nagy announces Hungary's neutrality and withdrawal from the Warsaw Pact. Soviet troops begin to re-enter Hungary, contrary to assurances by the Soviet government. János Kádár and Ferenc Münnich secretly defect to the Soviets.
The Springhill mining disaster in Springhill, Nova Scotia kills 39 miners; 88 are rescued.

main.desc: Any of three mining disasters in Springhill, Nova Scotia, Canada (1891, 1956, 1958)

events.text: The Mackinac Bridge, the world's longest suspension bridge between anchorages at the time, opens to traffic connecting Michigan's upper and lower peninsulas.
After being struck in the face with a hockey puck, Jacques Plante played the rest of the game wearing a face mask, now mandatory equipment for goaltenders in ice hockey.
Dominique Mbonyumutwa, one of the few Hutu sub-chiefs in colonial Rwanda, was attacked by Tutsi activists, precipitating the Rwandan Revolution.
Lê Quang Tung, loyalist head of the South Vietnam Special Forces, was executed in a U.S.-backed coup against president Ngô Đình Diệm following a period of religious unrest.

links.t: Army of the Republic of Vietnam Special Forces

events.text: The Arecibo Observatory in Arecibo, Puerto Rico, with the largest radio telescope ever constructed, officially opens.

main.desc: Radio observatory in Arecibo, Puerto Rico

events.text: The 1963 South Vietnamese coup begins.

main.desc: Military overthrow of President Ngô Đình Diệm

events.text: The Motion Picture Association of America's film rating system is officially introduced, originating with the ratings G, M, R, and X.

links.t: Motion Picture Association film rating system

events.text: Club Cinq-Sept fire in Saint-Laurent-du-Pont, France kills 146 young people.
Elvis on Tour, a concert film that documented Elvis Presley's tour throughout the United States, opened.
Watergate scandal: Leon Jaworski is appointed as the new Watergate Special Prosecutor.
The Indian state of Mysore is renamed as Karnataka to represent all the regions within Karunadu.
Burundian president Michel Micombero is deposed in a bloodless military coup d'état by deputy Jean-Baptiste Bagaza.
In Bolivia, Colonel Alberto Natusch executes a bloody coup d'état against the constitutional government of Wálter Guevara.
Griselda Álvarez becomes the first female governor of a state of Mexico.
Antigua and Barbuda gains independence from the United Kingdom.
Honda becomes the first Asian automobile company to produce cars in the United States with the opening of its factory in Marysville, Ohio; a Honda Accord is the first car produced there.
After the assassination of Indira Gandhi, Prime Minister of India on 31 October 1984, by two of her Sikh bodyguards, anti-Sikh riots erupt.
British Rail Class 43 (HST) hits the record speed of 238 km/h for rail vehicles with on-board fuel to generate electricity for traction motors.
President of the Chechen Republic Dzhokhar Dudayev declares sovereignty of the Chechen Republic of Ichkeria from the Russian Federation.
The Maastricht Treaty takes effect, formally establishing the European Union.

main.desc: 1992 founding treaty of the European Union

events.text: Titanic premieres publicly at Tokyo festival, launching a global blockbuster career.
Karl Bushby set off from Punta Arenas, Chile, beginning his attempt to walk around the world towards England, a journey that remains ongoing.
Chhattisgarh officially becomes the 26th state of India, formed from sixteen districts of eastern Madhya Pradesh.

links.t: States and union territories of India

events.text: Serbia and Montenegro joins the United Nations.
Turkey, Australia, and Canada agree to commit troops to the invasion of Afghanistan.

main.desc: Country in Southeastern Europe and West Asia

events.text: An Ilyushin Il-76 crashes near the Mir mine after takeoff from Mirny Airport in Yakutia, killing all 11 aboard.

main.desc: Russian heavy four-engined military transport jet aircraft

events.text: Mario Draghi succeeds Jean-Claude Trichet and becomes the third president of the European Central Bank.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Italy from 2021 to 2022

events.text: A fuel tank truck crashes and explodes in the Saudi Arabian capital Riyadh, killing 26 people and injuring 135.

main.t: List of tank truck fires and explosions

events.text: A concrete canopy collapses at the Novi Sad railway station, killing 16 people and injuring 3.

main.t: Novi Sad railway station canopy collapse

events.text: Emperor Gaozu of Tang allowed the assassination of a khagan of the Western Turkic Khaganate by Eastern Turkic rivals, one of the earliest events in the Tang campaigns against the Western Turks.

links.t: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks

events.text: A qaghan of the Western Turkic Khaganate is assassinated in a Chinese palace by Eastern Turkic rivals after the approval of Tang emperor Gaozu.

main.desc: Imperial title of Mongolic and Turkic societies

links.t: Tang campaigns against the Western Turks

events.text: The Peace of Bicêtre suspends hostilities in the Armagnac–Burgundian Civil War.
Plymouth Colony governor Josiah Winslow leads a colonial militia against the Narragansett during King Philip's War.
Four British naval vessels run aground on the Isles of Scilly because of faulty navigation. In response, the first Longitude Act is enacted in 1714.

main.desc: Royal Navy ship loss in storm

events.text: The French Directory, a five-man revolutionary government, is created.

main.desc: Executive power of the French Constitution of 1795–1799

events.text: Time zone: New Zealand officially adopts a standard time to be observed nationally.

main.desc: Area that observes a uniform standard time

events.text: James A. Garfield was elected as president of the United States; the election is the closest to date by popular vote margin.

main.desc: President of the United States in 1881

links.t: List of United States presidential elections by popular vote margin

events.text: The great fire destroys a large part of Oulu's city center in Oulu Province, Finland.
North Dakota and South Dakota are admitted as the 39th and 40th U.S. states.
The Boers begin their 118-day siege of British-held Ladysmith during the Second Boer War.

main.desc: Descendants of Afrikaners beyond the Cape Colony frontier

events.text: Bulgaria defeats the Ottoman Empire in the Battle of Lule Burgas, the bloodiest battle of the First Balkan War, which opens her way to Constantinople.

main.desc: State in southeastern Europe from 1908 to 1946

events.text: World War I: The Russian Empire declares war on the Ottoman Empire and the Dardanelles is subsequently closed.
The British government issued the Balfour Declaration in support of a Jewish homeland in Palestine, then an Ottoman region with a small Jewish minority.

The Balfour Declaration proclaims British support for the "establishment in Palestine of a national home for the Jewish people" with the clear understanding "that nothing shall be done which may prejudice the civil and religious rights of existing non-Jewish communities".
The Military Revolutionary Committee of the Petrograd Soviet, in charge of preparation and carrying out the Russian Revolution, holds its first meeting.

main.desc: Militant group of the Petrograd Soviet from November to December 1917

events.text: The Ocoee massacre commences in Orange County, Florida on the day of the 1920 United States presidential election.
In the United States, KDKA of Pittsburgh starts broadcasting as the first commercial radio station. The first broadcast is the result of the 1920 United States presidential election.

main.desc: Talk radio station in the Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania

events.text: The Australian military began a "war against emus", flightless native birds blamed for widespread damage to crops in Western Australia.
The BBC Television Service, the world's first regular, "high-definition" (then defined as at least 200 lines) service begins. Renamed BBC1 in 1964, the channel still runs to this day.
World War II: First day of Battle of Elaia–Kalamas between the Greeks and the Italians.
World War II: A U.S. Navy task force turned away an Imperial Japanese Navy formation at the Battle of Empress Augusta Bay, thus protecting the landings at Cape Torokina.

In California, designer Howard Hughes performs the maiden (and only) flight of the Hughes H-4 Hercules (also known as the "Spruce Goose"), the largest fixed-wing aircraft ever built until Scaled Composites rolled out their Stratolaunch in May 2017.

main.desc: American aviator, aerospace engineer and business magnate (1905–1976)

events.text: The Dutch–Indonesian Round Table Conference ended with the Netherlands agreeing to transfer sovereignty of the Dutch East Indies to the United States of Indonesia.
The Dutch–Indonesian Round Table Conference ends with the Netherlands agreeing to transfer sovereignty of the Dutch East Indies to the United States of Indonesia.

Canada in the Korean War: A platoon of The Royal Canadian Regiment defends a vital area against a full battalion of Chinese troops in the Battle of the Song-gok Spur. The engagement lasts into the early hours the next day.

main.desc: Aspect of Canadian military history from 1950 to 1953

events.text: Hungarian Revolution: Nikita Khrushchev meets with leaders of other Communist countries to seek their advice on the situation in Hungary, selecting János Kádár as the country's next leader on the advice of Josip Broz Tito.
Suez Crisis: Israel occupies the Gaza Strip.
A large number of people witnessed a fiery object in the sky near Levelland, Texas, which the United States Air Force said was ball lightning.

main.desc: UFO incident in Texas, United States in 1957

events.text: Quiz show scandals: Twenty-One game show contestant Charles Van Doren admits to a Congressional committee that he had been given questions and answers in advance.

main.desc: Secret collusion between contestants and producers

events.text: The first section of the M1 motorway, the first inter-urban motorway in the United Kingdom, is opened between the present junctions 5 and 18, along with the M10 motorway and M45 motorway.

main.desc: First inter-urban motorway in the UK

events.text: Penguin Books is found not guilty of obscenity in the trial R v Penguin Books Ltd, the Lady Chatterley's Lover case.
President Ngô Đình Diệm of South Vietnam was assassinated, marking the culmination of a coup d'état led by Dương Văn Minh.

main.desc: President of South Vietnam from 1955 to 1963

links.t: Arrest and assassination of Ngo Dinh Diem

events.text: South Vietnamese President Ngô Đình Diệm is assassinated following a military coup.

links.t: Arrest and assassination of Ngo Dinh Diem

events.text: King Saud of Saudi Arabia is deposed by a family coup, and replaced by his half-brother Faisal.

main.desc: King of Saudi Arabia from 1953 to 1964

events.text: Norman Morrison, a 31-year-old Quaker, sets himself on fire in front of the river entrance to the Pentagon to protest the use of napalm in the Vietnam war.
The Cuban Adjustment Act comes into force, allowing 123,000 Cubans the opportunity to apply for permanent residence in the United States.

main.desc: 1966 U.S. law to help Cuban immigrants become permanent residents

events.text: Vietnam War: US President Lyndon B. Johnson and "The Wise Men" conclude that the American people should be given more optimistic reports on the progress of the war.
Aeroflot Flight 19 is hijacked and diverted to Vnukovo International Airport, where the aircraft is stormed by authorities.

main.desc: 1973 airliner hijacking in the Soviet Union

events.text: Channel 4, the British free-to-air public broadcast television channel funded by its commercial activities, starts broadcasting.
U.S. President Ronald Reagan signs a bill creating Martin Luther King Jr. Day.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1981 to 1989

events.text: The serial killer Velma Barfield became the first woman to be executed in the United States since 1962.

links.t: Capital punishment in the United States

events.text: Capital punishment: Velma Barfield becomes the first woman executed in the United States since 1962.

main.desc: Legal killing of a person as punishment

events.text: Lebanon hostage crisis: U.S. hostage David Jacobsen is released in Beirut after 17 months in captivity.

main.desc: Kidnapping in Lebanon of 104 foreign hostages between 1982 and 1992

events.text: The Morris worm, the first Internet-distributed computer worm to gain significant mainstream media attention, is launched from MIT.
LOT Polish Airlines Flight 703 crashes in Białobrzegi, Podkarpackie Voivodeship, Poland, killing one person and injuring several more.
British Satellite Broadcasting and Sky Television plc merge to form BSkyB as a result of massive losses.
A lightning strike ruptured three oil tanks near Dronka, Egypt, causing a flood that killed 469 people.
Tropical Storm Linda made landfall in the Mekong Delta in Vietnam, causing more than 3,000 deaths.

main.desc: Pacific severe tropical storm and North Indian cyclone in 1997

events.text: Tropical Storm Linda makes landfall in the Mekong Delta in Vietnam, causing more than 3,000 deaths.

main.desc: Pacific severe tropical storm and North Indian cyclone in 1997

events.text: Honolulu shootings: In the worst mass murder in the history of Hawaii, a gunman shoots at eight people in his workplace, killing seven.

As members of Expedition 1, American astronaut William Shepherd and Russian cosmonauts Sergei Krikalev and Yuri Gidzenko (all pictured) became the first resident crew to arrive at the International Space Station.
Expedition 1 arrived at the International Space Station for the first long-duration stay onboard. From this day to present, a continuous human presence in space on the station remains uninterrupted.
Lewis Hamilton (pictured) overtook Timo Glock in the final corners of the Brazilian Grand Prix to win the Formula One championship by one point.

links.t: List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions

events.text: Lewis Hamilton secured his maiden Formula One Drivers' Championship Title by one point ahead of Felipe Massa at the Brazilian Grand Prix, after a pass for fifth place against the Toyota of Timo Glock on the final lap of the race.

links.t: List of Formula One World Drivers' Champions

events.text: The Chicago Cubs defeat the Cleveland Indians in the World Series, ending the longest Major League Baseball championship drought at 108 years.
In Vienna's Innere Stadt district, an ISIL sympathizer shoots and kills four people and injures 23 more, before being shot and killed by the police.

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Austria

events.text: A peace agreement is signed between the Ethiopian government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front, ending the Tigray War.
Emperor Constantius II dies of a fever at Mopsuestia in Cilicia; on his deathbed he is baptised and declares his cousin Julian rightful successor.
The Rouen Riot, an attempt by English king William Rufus to take possession of Rouen, the capital city of his brother Robert, duke of Normandy, fails.
The River Arno floods causing massive damage in Florence as recorded by the Florentine chronicler Giovanni Villani.
Liège is sacked by the troops of Duke Charles the Bold of Burgundy.

main.desc: Capital of Liège province, Wallonia, Belgium

events.text: Peace of Etaples between Henry VII of England and Charles VIII of France.

main.desc: Treaty between England and France in 1492

events.text: Christopher Columbus first sights the island of Dominica in the Caribbean Sea.
The Parliament of England passed the first Act of Supremacy, making King Henry VIII head of the Church of England, supplanting the pope and the Catholic Church.
English Parliament passes the first Act of Supremacy, making King Henry VIII head of the Anglican Church, supplanting the pope and the  Roman Catholic Church.
The American Continental Army is disbanded.

main.desc: Army of the United States from 1775 to 1784

events.text: The University of Vermont, the oldest university in Vermont, and fifth-oldest in New England, is chartered.

main.desc: Public university in Burlington, Vermont, U.S.

events.text: French Revolution: Playwright, journalist and outspoken feminist Olympe de Gouges  was guillotined.
French playwright, journalist and feminist Olympe de Gouges is guillotined.

main.desc: Range of socio-political movements and ideologies

events.text: War of the Third Coalition: The Treaty of Potsdam was signed compelling Prussia to join the coalition if it failed to negotiate peace between Russia and France.
French invasion of Russia: As Napoleon's Grande Armée began its retreat, its rear guard was defeated at the Battle of Vyazma.
Napoleon's armies are defeated at the Battle of Vyazma.
The Bank of Montreal, Canada's oldest chartered bank, opens in Montreal.

links.t: List of banks in the Americas

events.text: The Times of India, the world's largest circulated English language daily broadsheet newspaper is founded as The Bombay Times and Journal of Commerce.
A new constitution drafted by Johan Rudolph Thorbecke was proclaimed, limiting the powers of the Dutch monarchy.
A greatly revised Dutch constitution, which transfers much authority from the king to his parliament and ministers, is proclaimed.
Giuseppe Garibaldi and his followers are defeated in the Battle of Mentana and fail to end the Pope's Temporal power in Rome (it would be achieved three years later).

links.t: Temporal power of the Holy See

events.text: John Willis Menard (R-LA) becomes the first African American elected to the United States Congress.  Because of an electoral challenge, he is never seated.
The current melody of Kimigayo, the national anthem of Japan, was adopted.
Indigenous Mapuche began an uprising against the occupation of Araucanía by Chile.
The Mapuche uprising of 1881 begins in Chile.
The Fashoda Incident ended with French forces withdrawing after several months of military stalemate with the British in Fashoda (now in South Sudan).
France withdraws its troops from Fashoda (now in Sudan), ending the Fashoda Incident.

main.desc: Town in Greater Upper Nile, South Sudan

events.text: With the encouragement of the United States, Panama separates from Colombia.
William Howard Taft is elected the 27th President of the United States.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1909 to 1913

events.text: Chevrolet officially enters the automobile market in competition with the Ford Model T.

main.desc: American automobile division of General Motors

events.text: The German Revolution of 1918–19 begins when 40,000 sailors take over the port in Kiel.
Russian Civil War: The Russian Army retreats to Crimea, after a successful offensive by the Red Army and Revolutionary Insurgent Army of Ukraine.

main.desc: Multi-party war in the former Russian Empire (1917–1922)

events.text: The Gwangju Student Independence Movement occurred.
Getúlio Vargas becomes Head of the Provisional Government in Brazil after a bloodless coup on October 24.
Panagis Tsaldaris becomes the 142nd Prime Minister of Greece.

links.t: List of prime ministers of Greece

events.text: In a widely criticised referendum, almost 98 percent of Greek voters supported the restoration of George II (pictured) as King of the Hellenes.
George II of Greece regains his throne through a popular, though possibly fixed, plebiscite.
Franklin D. Roosevelt is reelected as President of the United States.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1933 to 1945

events.text: World War II: U.S. Marines and U.S. Army forces began an attempt to encircle and destroy a regiment of Imperial Japanese Army troops on Guadalcanal.
World War II: The Koli Point action begins during the Guadalcanal campaign and ends on November 12.
The Holocaust: The largest massacre of Jews by German forces began at Majdanek concentration camp.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: World War II: Five hundred aircraft of the U.S. 8th Air Force devastate Wilhelmshaven harbor in Germany.

main.t: Bombing of Wilhelmshaven in World War II

events.text: World War II: Two supreme commanders of the Slovak National Uprising, Generals Ján Golian and Rudolf Viest, are captured, tortured and later executed by German forces.
The Constitution of Japan is adopted through Emperor's assent.

The Chicago Daily Tribune published the erroneous headline "Dewey Defeats Truman" (pictured) in its early morning edition shortly after incumbent U.S. president Harry S. Truman officially upset the heavily favored governor of New York Thomas Dewey in the presidential election.
Chinese Civil War: The Battle of Dengbu Island occurs.

main.desc: 1949 battle of the Chinese Civil War

events.text: Air India Flight 245 crashes into Mont Blanc while on approach to Geneva Airport, killing all 48 people on board.
The first film featuring the giant monster known as Godzilla was released (poster pictured) nationwide in Japan.

main.desc: 1954 Japanese monster film by Ishirō Honda

events.text: Suez Crisis: During an invasion of the Gaza Strip, Israeli soldiers shot and killed hundreds of Palestinian refugees and local inhabitants in Khan Yunis.
Suez Crisis: The Khan Yunis killings by the Israel Defense Forces in Egyptian-controlled Gaza result in the deaths of 275 Palestinians.

Hungarian Revolution: A new Hungarian government is formed, in which many members of banned non-Communist parties participate.  János Kádár and Ferenc Münnich form a counter-government in Moscow as Soviet troops prepare for the final assault.
The Soviet Union launched Sputnik 2, carrying the space dog Laika as the first living creature to enter orbit around Earth.

main.desc: Second spacecraft launched into Earth orbit (1957)

main.desc: Index of lists with the same name

events.text: The land that would become the Great Swamp National Wildlife Refuge is established by an Act of Congress after a year-long legal battle that pitted local residents against Port Authority of New York and New Jersey officials wishing to turn the Great Swamp into a major regional airport for jet aircraft.

main.desc: Protected area in New Jersey, United States

links.t: Port Authority of New York and New Jersey

events.text: U Thant is unanimously appointed as the 3rd Secretary-General of the United Nations, becoming the first non-European individual to occupy the post.

Lyndon B. Johnson is elected to a full term as U.S. president, winning 61% of the vote and 44 states, while Washington D.C. residents are able to vote in a presidential election for the first time, casting the majority of their votes for Lyndon Johnson.

main.desc: North American federation of labor unions from 1935 to 1955

events.text: American fashion designer Ruth Harkness seeks and captures a nine-week-old panda cub in Sichuan; named Su Lin, he becomes the first live giant panda to enter the United States.

main.desc: American fashion designer, socialite, and panda owner

events.text: Second Sino-Japanese War: The Chinese Army withdraws from the Battle of Shanghai.

Kristallnacht occurs, instigated by the Nazis using the killing of German diplomat Ernst vom Rath by Herschel Grynszpan as justification.

Warsaw is awarded the Virtuti Militari by the Polish government-in-exile.

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Poland

main.desc: Major World War II battle from 1942 to 1943

events.text: An agreement for the founding of the United Nations Relief and Rehabilitation Administration is signed by 44 countries in the White House, Washington, D.C.

main.desc: Residence and workplace of the US president

events.text: Soo Bahk Do and Moo Duk Kwan martial arts are founded in Korea.
Cambodia gains independence from France.

Robert McNamara is named president of the Ford Motor Company, becoming the first non-Ford family member to serve in that post. He resigns a month later to join the newly elected John F. Kennedy administration.
At a coal mine in Miike, Japan, an explosion kills 458 and hospitalises 839 with carbon monoxide poisoning.

main.desc: Defunct coal mine in Kyushu, Japan

events.text: The Tsurumi rail accident on the Tōkaidō Main Line in Yokohama kills 162 people.
Several U.S. states and parts of Canada are hit by a series of blackouts lasting up to 13 hours in the Northeast blackout of 1965.

main.desc: Loss of electric power to an area

events.text: A Catholic Worker Movement member, Roger Allen LaPorte, protesting against the Vietnam War, sets himself on fire in front of the United Nations building.

main.desc: Autonomous communities of Catholics and their associates

events.text: The first issue of Rolling Stone, an American magazine focusing on music, politics and popular culture, was published.
Apollo program: NASA launches the unmanned Apollo 4 test spacecraft, atop the first Saturn V rocket, from Florida's Cape Kennedy.

links.t: Supreme Court of the United States

events.text: American banker John List murdered his wife, mother, and three children with a pair of handguns.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

East German official Günter Schabowski mistakenly announced the immediate opening of the inner German border, resulting in the fall of the Berlin Wall that night (border crossing pictured).

main.desc: Bridge in Mostar, Bosnia and Herzegovina

events.text: The chemical element darmstadtium is discovered.

main.desc: Chemical substance not composed of simpler ones

events.text: A U.S. federal judge, in the largest civil settlement in American history, orders 37 U.S. brokerage houses to pay US$1.03 billion to cheated NASDAQ investors to compensate for price fixing.
Capital punishment in the United Kingdom, already abolished for murder, is completely abolished for all remaining capital offences.

main.t: Capital punishment in the United Kingdom
main.desc: History of the death penalty in the United Kingdom

events.text: TAESA Flight 725 crashes after takeoff from Uruapan International Airport in Uruapan, Michoacán, Mexico, killing all 18 people on board.
Uttarakhand officially becomes the 27th state of India, formed from thirteen districts of northwestern Uttar Pradesh.

links.t: States and union territories of India

events.text: Firefox 1.0 is released.
The Venus Express mission of the European Space Agency is launched from the Baikonur Cosmodrome in Kazakhstan.
Suicide bombers attack three hotels in Amman, Jordan, killing at least 60 people.
The first national test of the Emergency Alert System is activated in the United States at 2:00 p.m. EST.

main.desc: Method of emergency broadcasting in the United States

events.text: A train carrying liquid fuel crashes and bursts into flames in northern Myanmar, killing 27 people and injuring 80 others.
At least 27 people are killed and dozens are wounded in conflicts between inmates and guards at Welikada prison in Colombo.

main.desc: Prison riot in Colombo, Sri Lanka

events.text: A non-binding self-determination consultation is held in Catalonia, asking Catalan citizens their opinion on whether Catalonia should become a state and, if so, whether it should be an independent state.

main.desc: Referendum in the Spanish region of Catalonia

events.text: A tram derailment in Croydon, London, killed seven people.
Pakistani prime minister Imran Khan inaugurated the Kartarpur Corridor, a visa-free border crossing connecting the Gurdwara Darbar Sahib to the India–Pakistan border.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Pakistan from 2018 to 2022

events.text: The Alabama Crimson Tide and LSU Tigers football teams, both with undefeated records thus far that season, played in a "Game of the Century".
Second Nagorno-Karabakh War: An armistice agreement is signed by Armenia, Azerbaijan and Russia.
U.S. surgeons at NYU Langone Health announce the world's first whole eye transplant.

main.desc: Hospital in New York, United States

Ten Kingdoms: Li Bian usurps the throne and deposes Emperor Yang Pu. The Wu State is replaced by Li (now called "Xu Zhigao"), who becomes the first ruler of Southern Tang.

main.t: Five Dynasties and Ten Kingdoms period

Raden Wijaya is crowned as the first monarch of Majapahit kingdom of Java, taking the throne name Kertarajasa Jayawardhana.

main.desc: 13th-century Javanese emperor, the founder and the first monarch of Majapahit empire

events.text: Battle of Varna: The crusading forces of King Władysław III of Poland (aka Ulaszlo I of Hungary and Władysław III of Varna) are defeated by the Turks under Sultan Murad II and Władysław is killed.

main.desc: Battle in the Crusade of Varna

events.text: At the culmination of a Swedish civil war, supporters of the deposed King Sigismund III Vasa were publicly executed in the Åbo Bloodbath.

main.desc: Ruler of Poland–Lithuania (1587–1632), King of Sweden (1592–1599)

Chattrapati Shivaji Maharaj, Maratha King kills Afzal Khan, Adilshahi in the battle popularly known as Battle of Pratapgarh.

main.desc: Chhatrapati of the Marathas from 1674 to 1680

events.text: Third Anglo-Dutch War: As provided in the Treaty of Westminster, Netherlands cedes New Netherland to England.

main.desc: 1672–74 war related to the Franco-Dutch War

events.text: English colonists under the command of James Moore besiege Spanish St. Augustine during Queen Anne's War.
The last colonial governor of New Jersey, William Franklin, signs the charter of Queen's College (later renamed Rutgers University).
The United States Marine Corps is founded at Tun Tavern in Philadelphia by Samuel Nicholas.

main.desc: Naval infantry branch of the U.S. military

events.text: A Goddess of Reason is proclaimed by the French Convention at the suggestion of Pierre Gaspard Chaumette.
Cry of Independence by Rufina Alfaro at La Villa de Los Santos, Panama setting into motion a revolt which led to Panama's independence from Spain and to it immediately becoming part of Colombia.
The passenger ship Stephen Whitney is wrecked in thick fog off the southern coast of Ireland, killing 92 of the 110 on board. The disaster results in the construction of the Fastnet Rock lighthouse.

main.desc: American passenger and cargo ship; wrecked off the southern Irish coast in 1847

main.desc: Confederate States Army officer and doctor (1823–1865)

main.desc: Confederate States Army officer and doctor (1823–1865)

events.text: Journalist and explorer Henry Morton Stanley (pictured) located missing missionary and explorer David Livingstone near Lake Tanganyika in present-day Tanzania.
Henry Morton Stanley locates missing explorer and missionary, David Livingstone in Ujiji, near Lake Tanganyika, famously greeting him with the words, "Dr. Livingstone, I presume?"

White supremacists seized power and massacred black Americans during the Wilmington massacre,(newspaper headline depicted) the only instance of a municipal government being overthrown in United States history.

main.desc: Belief in the superiority of white people

main.desc: Belief in the superiority of white people

events.text: The date of Thomas A. Davis' opening of the San Diego Army and Navy Academy, although the official founding date is November 23, 1910.

The Western Union Cable Office in North Sydney, Nova Scotia, receives a top-secret coded message from Europe (that would be sent to Ottawa and Washington, D.C.) that said on November 11, 1918, all fighting would cease on land, sea and in the air.
Brazilian president Getúlio Vargas led a coup against his own constitutional government, establishing the dictatorial Estado Novo regime.
Finnish author F. E. Sillanpää is awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
An earthquake registering 7.7 Mw struck the Vrancea region of Romania.
The 1940 Vrancea earthquake strikes Romania killing an estimated 1,000 and injuring approximately 4,000 more.
World War II: Germany invades Vichy France following French Admiral François Darlan's agreement to an armistice with the Allies in North Africa.
The ammunition ship USS Mount Hood explodes at Seeadler Harbour, Manus, Admiralty Islands, killing at least 432 and wounding 371.
Indonesian National Revolution: Following the killing of Brigadier A. W. S. Mallaby on 30 October, British forces retaliated by attacking Surabaya (present-day logo depicted).

main.desc: 1945–1949 Indonesian conflict and diplomatic struggle against Dutch rule

events.text: Heavy fighting in Surabaya between Indonesian nationalists and returning colonialists after World War II, today celebrated as Heroes' Day (Hari Pahlawan).

main.desc: Battle between British and Indonesian forces

events.text: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake in the Peruvian Andes mountains kills at least 1,400 people.
With the rollout of the North American Numbering Plan, direct-dial coast-to-coast telephone service begins in the United States.

main.desc: Integrated telephone numbering plan of twenty North American countries

events.text: U.S. President Dwight D. Eisenhower dedicates the USMC War Memorial (Iwo Jima memorial) in Arlington Ridge Park in Arlington County, Virginia.

main.desc: World War II general, U.S. president from 1953 to 1961

events.text: The Hope Diamond is donated to the Smithsonian Institution by New York diamond merchant Harry Winston.
The Nauru Independence Act 1967 passed the Parliament of Australia, giving independence to the UN Trust Territory of Nauru with effect from 31 January 1968.

main.desc: Legal Act of Independence of Nauru

events.text: The children's television series Sesame Street premiered in the United States.
National Educational Television (the predecessor to the Public Broadcasting Service) in the United States debuts Sesame Street.
Vietnam War: Vietnamization: For the first time in five years, an entire week ends with no reports of American combat fatalities in Southeast Asia.
Luna 17: uncrewed space mission launched by the Soviet Union.
In Cambodia, Khmer Rouge forces attack the city of Phnom Penh and its airport, killing 44, wounding at least 30 and damaging nine aircraft.
A Merpati Nusantara Airlines Vickers Viscount crashes into the Indian Ocean near Padang, West Sumatra, Indonesia, killing all 69 people on board.

links.t: 1971 Merpati Nusantara Airlines Vickers Viscount crash

events.text: Southern Airways Flight 49 from Birmingham, Alabama is hijacked and, at one point, is threatened with crashing into the nuclear installation at the Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After two days, the plane lands in Havana, Cuba, where the hijackers are jailed by Fidel Castro.
In Angola, the MPLA decisively defeated the FNLA in the Battle of Quifangondo, while Portugal simultaneously withdrew all its colonial and military personnel from Luanda.
SS Edmund Fitzgerald sank in Lake Superior, claiming all 29 of her crew's lives.

main.desc: Great Lakes freighter sunk in Lake Superior

events.text: The 729-foot-long freighter SS Edmund Fitzgerald sinks during a storm on Lake Superior, killing all 29 crew on board.

main.desc: Great Lakes freighter sunk in Lake Superior

events.text: Treaty of Osimo between Yugoslavia and Italy
Israeli-Palestinian conflict: the United Nations General Assembly passes Resolution 3379, determining that Zionism is a form of racism.

main.desc: Ongoing military and political conflict in West Asia

events.text: A 106-car Canadian Pacific freight train carrying explosive and poisonous chemicals from Windsor, Ontario, Canada derails in Mississauga, Ontario.

main.desc: Class I railway in Canada and the United States

events.text: Bill Gates introduces Windows 1.0.
A Dassault Falcon 50 and a Piper PA-28 Cherokee collide in mid-air over Fairview, New Jersey, killing six people and injuring eight.

main.desc: Midsize three engine long range business jet

events.text: Longtime Bulgarian leader Todor Zhivkov is removed from office and replaced by Petar Mladenov.
Germans begin to tear down the Berlin Wall.
Writer and environmental activist Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight others from the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People were executed by the Nigerian military regime led by Sani Abacha.

links.t: Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People

events.text: In Nigeria, playwright and environmental activist Ken Saro-Wiwa, along with eight others from the Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (Mosop), are hanged by government forces.

links.t: Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People

events.text: WorldCom and MCI Communications announce a $37 billion merger (the largest merger in US history at the time).
World Anti-Doping Agency is formed in Lausanne.

main.desc: Foundation created by the International Olympic Committee

events.text: Veteran's Day Weekend Tornado Outbreak: A tornado outbreak stretching from Northern Ohio to the Gulf Coast, one of the largest outbreaks recorded in November.

main.desc: Severe weather event in the eastern United States

events.text: Nadarajah Raviraj, a prominent Sri Lankan Tamil politician and human rights lawyer, was assassinated in Colombo.
Sri Lankan Tamil politician Nadarajah Raviraj is assassinated in Colombo.

The National Museum of the Marine Corps in Quantico, Virginia is opened and dedicated by U.S. President George W. Bush, who announces that Marine Corporal Jason Dunham will posthumously receive the Medal of Honor.

main.t: National Museum of the Marine Corps
main.desc: Museum in Triangle, Virginia, United States

events.text: At the Ibero-American Summit in Santiago, Chile, King Juan Carlos I of Spain asked Venezuelan president Hugo Chávez "Why don't you shut up?" after Chávez repeatedly interrupted a speech by Spanish prime minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero.

main.desc: Meeting for Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries

events.text: Over five months after landing on Mars, NASA declares the Phoenix mission concluded after communications with the lander were lost.
A skirmish occurred between South Korean and North Korean naval ships off Daecheong Island in the Yellow Sea.

main.desc: 2009 South and North Korean naval skirmish

main.desc: 2009 South and North Korean naval skirmish

events.text: President of Bolivia Evo Morales and several of his government resign after 19 days of civil protests and a recommendation from the military.
The British government announced that it had removed the last land mine from the Falkland Islands, laid by Argentine forces during the 1982 Falklands War.

main.t: Land mines in the Falkland Islands

events.text: Armenia and Azerbaijan sign a ceasefire agreement, ending the Second Nagorno-Karabakh War, and prompting protests in Armenia.

At Carnuntum, Emperor emeritus Diocletian confers with Galerius, Augustus of the East, and Maximianus, the recently returned former Augustus of the West, in an attempt to end the civil wars of the Tetrarchy.

main.desc: Ancient Roman military outpost in modern Austria

events.text: Constantine VIII dies, ending his uninterrupted reign as emperor or co-emperor of the Byzantine Empire of 66 years.
Henry I of England marries Matilda of Scotland, the daughter of Malcolm III of Scotland and a direct descendant of the Saxon king Edmund Ironside; Matilda is crowned on the same day.
The Fourth Council of the Lateran meets, defining the doctrine of transubstantiation, the process by which bread and wine are, by that doctrine, said to transform into the body and blood of Christ.
Treaty of Granada: Louis XII of France and Ferdinand II of Aragon agree to divide the Kingdom of Naples between them.

main.desc: Partition of Kingdom of Naples between France and Aragon

events.text: Tycho Brahe observes the supernova SN 1572.

main.desc: First governing document of Plymouth Colony

events.text: Following pressure from Anglican bishop John Atherton, the Irish House of Commons passes An Act for the Punishment for the Vice of Buggery.

Second Battle of Khotyn in Ukraine: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth forces under the command of Jan Sobieski defeat the Ottoman army. In this battle, rockets made by Kazimierz Siemienowicz are successfully used.

main.desc: Part of the Polish–Ottoman War of 1672–76

events.text: Gottfried Leibniz demonstrates integral calculus for the first time to find the area under the graph of y = ƒ(x).
Joseph Blake, alias Blueskin, a highwayman known for attacking "Thief-Taker General" (and thief) Jonathan Wild at the Old Bailey, is hanged in London.
Riots break out in Lhasa after the murder of the Tibetan regent.

main.desc: Uprising against Qing rule in Tibet

main.desc: 1778 massarce of the American Revolutionary War

main.desc: 1803–1815 series of wars led by Napoleon

In Jerusalem, Virginia, Nat Turner is hanged after inciting a violent slave uprising.

main.desc: Public college in Lexington, Virginia, US

Treaty of Sinchula is signed whereby Bhutan cedes the areas east of the Teesta River to the British East India Company.

main.desc: War fought between British India and Bhutan in 1864–1865

Many cities in the Midwestern United States break their record highs and lows on the same day as a strong cold front rolls through.

The Industrial Workers of the World attack an Armistice Day parade in Centralia, Washington, ultimately resulting in the deaths of five people.
Latvian forces defeat the West Russian Volunteer Army at Riga in the Latvian War of Independence.

main.desc: Russian warlords in the Baltic during the Russian Civil War

main.t: Tomb of the Unknown Soldier (Arlington National Cemetery)

events.text: Independence of Angola.

Antigua and Barbuda joins the United Nations.

main.desc: Legislatures of the constituent republics of the Soviet Union

events.text: Peter I of Cyprus ascends the throne of Cyprus after his father, Hugh IV of Cyprus, abdicates.
