Anglo-Scottish Wars: English forces captured about 1,200 Scots at the Battle of Solway Moss.

main.desc: Wars and battles between England and Scotland

events.text: Battle of Solway Moss: An English army defeats a much larger Scottish force near the River Esk in Dumfries and Galloway.
Abel Tasman becomes the first European to discover the island Van Diemen's Land (later renamed Tasmania).
Thirty Years' War: Holy Roman Empire, Bavarian and Spanish forces led by Franz von Mercy defeated the French army in Germany led by Marshal Josias von Rantzau at the Battle of Tuttlingen.
Tarabai, regent of the Maratha Empire, imprisons Rajaram II of Satara for refusing to remove Balaji Baji Rao from the post of peshwa.

main.desc: Regent of the Maratha Empire from 1700 to 1708

events.text: South Carolina passes the Ordinance of Nullification, declaring that the Tariffs of 1828 and 1832 were null and void in the state, beginning the Nullification Crisis.
The Texas Provincial Government authorizes the creation of a horse-mounted police force called the Texas Rangers (which is now the Texas Ranger Division of the Texas Department of Public Safety).

main.t: History of the Texas Ranger Division

events.text: Danish troops defeat a Schleswig-Holstein force in the town of Lottorf, Schleswig-Holstein.

main.desc: Part of the First Schleswig War

events.text: British naturalist Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species was first published, and sold out its initial print run on the first day.
British naturalist Charles Darwin's On the Origin of Species is published.
American Civil War: As part of the Chattanooga campaign in Chattanooga, Tennessee, Union forces captured Lookout Mountain, helping them to begin breaking the Confederate siege of the city.

American Civil War: Battle of Lookout Mountain: Near Chattanooga, Tennessee, Union forces under General Ulysses S. Grant capture Lookout Mountain and begin to break the Confederate siege of the city led by General Braxton Bragg.
Anna Sewell's animal welfare novel Black Beauty is published.
The second of two games between two Ohio football teams took place, after which accusations were made that players conspired to deliberately lose games.

A 13–6 victory by the Massillon Tigers over their rivals, the Canton Bulldogs, for the "Ohio League" Championship, leads to accusations that the championship series was fixed and results in the first major scandal in professional American football.

main.desc: Early professional football team from Masillon, Ohio

events.text: In Milwaukee, nine members of the Milwaukee Police Department are killed by a bomb, the most deaths in a single event in U.S. police history until the September 11 attacks in 2001.

main.desc: Largest city in Wisconsin, United States

events.text: The Podgorica Assembly convened in Montenegro, with the intention of uniting with the Kingdom of Serbia.
Irish Civil War: Irish nationalist author Erskine Childers was executed by the Irish Free State for illegally carrying a semi-automatic pistol.

main.desc: 1922–1923 conflict between factions of the IRA

events.text: Nine Irish Republican Army members are executed by an Irish Free State firing squad. Among them is author Erskine Childers, who had been arrested for illegally carrying a revolver.

links.t: Executions during the Irish Civil War

events.text: The Eugene O'Neill Theatre (pictured) opened on Broadway, New York, with a production of the musical Mayflowers.

main.desc: Broadway theater in Manhattan, New York

events.text: The Finnish far-right Lapua Movement officially begins when a group of mainly the former White Guard members, led by Vihtori Kosola, interrupted communism occasion at the Workers' House in Lapua, Finland.
In Washington, D.C., the FBI Scientific Crime Detection Laboratory (better known as the FBI Crime Lab) officially opens.
The Senegalese Socialist Party holds its second congress.

main.desc: Left-wing political party in Senegal during the 1930s

events.text: World War II: The First Slovak Republic becomes a signatory to the Tripartite Pact, officially joining the Axis powers.

The Holocaust: The Theresienstadt Ghetto was founded as a waystation to Nazi extermination camps and a "retirement settlement" for elderly and prominent Jews to mislead their communities about the Final Solution.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: World War II: The United States grants Lend-Lease to the Free French Forces.

main.desc: WWII program to provide U.S. allies with free armaments

events.text: World War II: Following the American capture of Makin Atoll, USS Liscome Bay was sunk by a torpedo from Japanese submarine I-175, killing 644.
World War II: At the battle of Makin the USS Liscome Bay is torpedoed near Tarawa and sinks, killing 650 men.

main.desc: Battle of the Pacific Theater of World War II

events.text: World War II: The 73rd Bombardment Wing launches the first attack on Tokyo from the Northern Mariana Islands.

main.desc: Inactive United States Air Force unit

events.text: The "Great Appalachian Storm", a large extratropical cyclone, struck the east coast of the United States before moving northeast.
Cold War: The West Berlin branch of the Socialist Unity Party of Germany forms a separate party, the Socialist Unity Party of West Berlin.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

links.t: Socialist Unity Party of West Berlin

events.text: The influential British satirical television programme That Was the Week That Was is first broadcast.

main.t: That Was the Week That Was

events.text: During a live television broadcast, businessman Jack Ruby shot and fatally wounded Lee Harvey Oswald, who assassinated U.S. president John F. Kennedy, fueling numerous conspiracy theories.

main.desc: American nightclub owner and murderer of Lee Harvey Oswald (1911–1967)

links.t: John F. Kennedy assassination conspiracy theories

events.text: Lee Harvey Oswald, the assassin of President John F. Kennedy, is killed by Jack Ruby on live television. Robert H. Jackson takes a photograph of the shooting that will win the 1964 Pulitzer Prize in Photography.

Joseph-Désiré Mobutu seizes power in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and becomes President; he rules the country (which he renames Zaire in 1971) for over 30 years, until being overthrown by rebels in 1997.

main.desc: President of DR Congo and Zaire from 1965 to 1997

links.t: List of presidents of the Democratic Republic of the Congo

events.text: Bulgarian TABSO Flight 101 crashes near Bratislava, Czechoslovakia, killing all 82 people on board.
Apollo program: The Apollo 12 command module splashes down safely in the Pacific Ocean, ending the second crewed mission to land on the Moon.
After collecting a ransom payout of $200,000, D. B. Cooper (depicted) parachuted out of the rear stairway of the airplane he had hijacked over the Pacific Northwest and disappeared.

During a severe thunderstorm over Washington state, a hijacker calling himself Dan Cooper (aka D. B. Cooper) parachutes from a Northwest Orient Airlines plane with $200,000 in ransom money. He has never been found.
A national speed limit is imposed on the Autobahn in Germany because of the 1973 oil crisis. The speed limit lasts only four months.

Donald Johanson and Tom Gray discover the 40% complete Australopithecus afarensis skeleton, nicknamed "Lucy" (after The Beatles song "Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds"), in the Awash Valley of Ethiopia's Afar Depression.

links.t: Lucy in the Sky with Diamonds

events.text: A magnitude-7.3 earthquake struck eastern Turkey, destroying 80 per cent of buildings in the region and causing at least 4,000 casualties.
The Çaldıran–Muradiye earthquake in eastern Turkey kills between 4,000 and 5,000 people.

After a week of mass protests against the Communist regime known as the Velvet Revolution, Miloš Jakeš and the entire Politburo of the Czechoslovak Communist Party resign from office.  This brings an effective end to Communist rule in Czechoslovakia.
Space Shuttle program: Atlantis launches on STS-44.
China Southern Airlines Flight 3943 crashes on approach to Guilin Qifengling Airport in Guilin, China, killing all 141 people on board.
Crossair Flight 3597 crashes in Bassersdorf near Zurich Airport, killing 24 people, including singer Melanie Thornton and two members of the German band Passion Fruit.
The Avdhela Project, an Aromanian digital library and cultural initiative, was launched in Bucharest, Romania.

main.desc: Aromanian digital library and cultural initiative

events.text: The Avdhela Project, an Aromanian digital library and cultural initiative, is founded in Bucharest, Romania.

main.desc: Aromanian digital library and cultural initiative

events.text: A fire at a clothing factory in Dhaka, Bangladesh, kills at least 112 people.
Iran signs an interim agreement with the P5+1 countries, limiting its nuclear program in exchange for reduced sanctions.
A Russian Sukhoi Su-24 attack aircraft was shot down by a Turkish fighter jet after the former allegedly strayed into Turkish airspace and ignored warnings to change course.

A Russian Air Force Sukhoi Su-24 fighter jet is shot down by the Turkish Air Force over the Syria–Turkey border, killing one of the two pilots; a Russian marine is also killed during a subsequent rescue effort.

main.desc: Branch of the Russian Aerospace Forces

events.text: A terrorist attack on a hotel in Al-Arish, Egypt, kills at least seven people and injures 12 others.
An explosion on a bus carrying Tunisian Presidential Guard personnel in Tunisia's capital Tunis leaves at least 14 people dead.

main.desc: Islamic State terror attack in Tunisia

events.text: The government of Colombia and the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia–People's Army sign a revised peace deal, bringing an end to the country's more than 50-year-long civil war.
A terrorist attack on a Mosque in Al-Rawda, North Sinai, Egypt kills 311 people and injures 128.

main.desc: Terrorist bombing in a Sinai mosque, Egypt

events.text: Five days after the general elections which resulted in a hung parliament, opposition leader and former deputy prime minister Anwar Ibrahim is officially named as the 10th prime minister of Malaysia.
Hibiscus Rising (pictured), a sculpture commemorating the life of David Oluwale, was unveiled in Leeds.

main.desc: Sculpture by Yinka Shonibare in Leeds

events.text: Hibiscus Rising, commemorating David Oluwale, is unveiled in Leeds.

main.desc: Sculpture by Yinka Shonibare in Leeds

events.text: Servius Tullius, king of Rome, celebrates the first of his three triumphs for his victory over the Etruscans.

main.desc: King of Rome from c. 578 to 535 BC

events.text: After Malcolm II of Scotland died at Glamis, Duncan, the son of his second daughter, rather than Macbeth, the son of his eldest daughter, inherited the throne to become the King of Scots.
Máel Coluim mac Cináeda, King of Scots, dies. His grandson, Donnchad, son of Bethóc and Crínán of Dunkeld, inherits the throne.
The White Ship sinks in the English Channel, drowning William Adelin, son and heir of Henry I of England.

main.desc: 12th-century shipwreck, killing the heir to the English throne

events.text: Baldwin IV of Jerusalem and Raynald of Châtillon defeat Saladin at the Battle of Montgisard.
A tsunami, caused by an earthquake in the Tyrrhenian Sea, devastates Naples and the Maritime Republic of Amalfi, among other places.
King Minkhaung I becomes king of Ava.
Elizabeth of York is crowned Queen Consort of England.
Reconquista: The Granada War was effectively brought to an end with the signing of the Treaty of Granada between Castile-Aragon and the Emirate of Granada.
The siege of Granada, the last Moorish stronghold in Spain, ends with the Treaty of Granada.
Adil Shahi–Portuguese conflicts: Afonso de Albuquerque, the governor of Portuguese India, led an armada to conquer Goa.

Portuguese conquest of Goa: Portuguese naval forces under the command of Afonso de Albuquerque, and local mercenaries working for privateer Timoji, seize Goa from the Bijapur Sultanate, resulting in 451 years of Portuguese colonial rule.
The Cudgel War begins in Finland (at the time part of Sweden), when peasants rebel against the imposition of taxes by the nobility.
A deadly earthquake rocks Shemakha in the Caucasus, killing 80,000 people.

main.desc: 1667 seismic event centered near present-day Shamakhi, Azerbaijan

events.text: Trunajaya rebellion: After a series of difficult marches, allied Mataram and Dutch troops successfully assaulted the rebel stronghold of Kediri in eastern Java.
Trunajaya rebellion: After a long and logistically challenging march, the allied Mataram and Dutch troops successfully assault the rebel stronghold of Kediri.
King Ferdinand VI of Spain grants royal protection to the Beaterio de la Compañia de Jesus, now known as the Congregation of the Religious of the Virgin Mary.
French and Indian War: British forces capture Fort Duquesne from French control. Later, Fort Pitt will be built nearby and grow into modern Pittsburgh.

main.desc: North American theater of the Seven Years' War

events.text: The second of two strong earthquakes struck the Levant and destroyed all the villages in the Beqaa Valley.
An earthquake hits the Mediterranean destroying Beirut and Damascus and killing 30,000–40,000.
American Revolutionary War: The last British troops leave New York City, three months after the signing of the Treaty of Paris.
Stanisław II Augustus (pictured), the last king of Poland, was forced to abdicate after the Third Partition of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth.
Partitions of Poland: Stanisław August Poniatowski, the last king of independent Poland, is forced to abdicate and is exiled to Russia.

main.desc: 18th-century forced partitions of the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth

events.text: The Greek frigate Hellas arrives in Nafplion to become the first flagship of the Hellenic Navy.

main.desc: Flagship of the Revolutionary Hellenic Navy (in service 1825–31)

events.text: A massive undersea earthquake, estimated magnitude between 8.7 and 9.2, rocks Sumatra, producing a massive tsunami all along the Indonesian coast.
A cyclone slams into south-eastern India.  An estimated 300,000 deaths resulted from the disaster.

main.desc: Devastating tropical cyclone that affected the town of Coringa

events.text: American Civil War: Confederate forces were defeated at the Battle of Missionary Ridge in Chattanooga, Tennessee, opening the door to the Union's invasion of the Deep South.

American Civil War: Battle of Missionary Ridge: Union forces led by General Ulysses S. Grant break the Siege of Chattanooga by routing Confederate troops under General Braxton Bragg at Missionary Ridge in Tennessee.

American Civil War: A group of Confederate operatives calling themselves the Confederate Army of Manhattan starts fires in more than 20 locations in an unsuccessful attempt to burn down New York City.
The United States Greenback Party is established as a political party consisting primarily of farmers affected by the Panic of 1873.

American Indian Wars: In retaliation for the American defeat at the Battle of the Little Bighorn, United States Army troops sack the sleeping village of Cheyenne Chief Dull Knife at the headwaters of the Powder River.

main.desc: Frontier conflicts in the United States, 1609–1890s

events.text: Banff National Park (pictured), the oldest national park in Canada, was established as the Banff Hot Springs Reserve.
Gustav Mahler's Symphony No. 4 premiered in Munich.
Prince Carl of Denmark arrives in Norway to become King Haakon VII of Norway.
A fire breaks out on SS Sardinia as it leaves Malta's Grand Harbour, resulting in the ship's grounding and the deaths of at least 118 people.
Românul de la Pind, the longest-running newspaper by and about Aromanians prior to World War II, ceases its publications.
Albert Einstein presents the field equations of general relativity to the Prussian Academy of Sciences.
World War I: German troops invaded Portuguese East Africa in an attempt to escape superior British forces to the north and resupply from captured Portuguese materiel.
World War I: German forces defeat Portuguese army of about 1,200 at Negomano on the border of modern-day Mozambique and Tanzania.
Vojvodina, formerly Austro-Hungarian crown land, proclaims its secession from Austria-Hungary to join the Kingdom of Serbia.
The deadliest November tornado outbreak in U.S. history kills 76 people and injures more than 400.

main.t: List of North American tornadoes and tornado outbreaks

events.text: Wilhelm Schäfer leaves the Nazi Party and hands over the Boxheim Documents to the Frankfurt police.

Nazi Germany and the Empire of Japan signed the Anti-Comintern Pact, agreeing that, if the Soviet Union attacked one of them, they would consult each other on what measures to take to "safeguard their common interests".

main.desc: 1936 treaty signed by Germany and Japan

events.text: In Berlin, Germany and Japan sign the Anti-Comintern Pact, agreeing to consult on measures "to safeguard their common interests" in the case of an unprovoked attack by the Soviet Union against either nation.

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Germany

events.text: The de Havilland Mosquito, one of the most successful military aircraft in the Second World War, made its first flight.

main.desc: British multi-role combat aircraft of WW2

events.text: World War II:  HMS Barham is sunk by a German torpedo.
World War II: Statehood of Bosnia and Herzegovina is re-established at the State Anti-fascist Council for the National Liberation of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

links.t: State Anti-fascist Council for the National Liberation of Bosnia and Herzegovina

events.text: McCarthyism: Executives from movie studios agreed to blacklist ten screenwriters and directors who were jailed for refusing to give testimony to the House Un-American Activities Committee.

main.desc: Phenomenon of US political rhetoric after WWII

events.text: Red Scare: The "Hollywood Ten" are blacklisted by Hollywood movie studios.

main.desc: Phenomenon of US political rhetoric after WWII

events.text: New Zealand ratifies the Statute of Westminster and thus becomes independent of legislative control by the United Kingdom.

main.desc: Law recognising autonomy of British Dominions

events.text: The Great Appalachian Storm of 1950 impacts 22 American states, killing 353 people, injuring over 160, and causing US$66.7 million in damages (1950 dollars).

The left-wing Japanese novelist Wataru Kaji disappeared, leading to a government inquiry in which CIA involvement was investigated; Kaji stated he was kidnapped and held against his will by intelligence officers, which the United States denied.
Korean War: After 42 days of fighting, the Battle of Triangle Hill ended as American and South Korean units abandoned their attempt to capture the "Iron Triangle".

Agatha Christie's murder-mystery play The Mousetrap opens at the Ambassadors Theatre in London's West End after a premiere in Nottingham, UK.  It will become the longest continuously running play in history.

links.t: List of the longest-running West End shows

events.text: Korean War: After 42 days of fighting, the Battle of Triangle Hill ends in a Chinese victory. American and South Korean units abandon their attempt to capture the "Iron Triangle".
French Sudan gains autonomy as a self-governing member of the French Community.
Three of the four Mirabal sisters, who opposed the dictatorship of military strongman Rafael Trujillo in the Dominican Republic, were beaten and strangled to death.
The Mirabal sisters of the Dominican Republic are assassinated.

State funeral of John F. Kennedy; after lying in state at the United States Capitol, a Requiem Mass takes place at Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle and the President is buried at Arlington National Cemetery.

main.t: State funeral of John F. Kennedy

links.t: Cathedral of St. Matthew the Apostle

events.text: The Old Student House in Helsinki, Finland is occupied by a large group of University of Helsinki students.

main.desc: Former student house of the Student Union of the University of Helsinki

events.text: After failing to instigate a military coup to restore the powers of the Emperor of Japan, author Yukio Mishima and a member of his militia committed ritual suicide.

main.desc: Attempted coup d'état in Japan on November 25, 1970, by writer Yukio Mishima

events.text: In Japan, author Yukio Mishima and one compatriot commit ritualistic seppuku after an unsuccessful coup attempt.

main.desc: Japanese author and coup attempt leader (1925–1970)

events.text: Georgios Papadopoulos, head of the military Regime of the Colonels in Greece, is ousted in a hardliners' coup led by Brigadier General Dimitrios Ioannidis.
Upon Suriname's independence from the Netherlands, Johan Ferrier (pictured) became its first president.
Coup of 25 November 1975, a failed military coup d'état by Portuguese far-left activists seeking to hijack the  Portuguese transition to democracy to establish a communist regime.
Suriname gains independence from the Netherlands.
Former Senator Benigno Aquino Jr., is found guilty by the Philippine Military Commission No. 2 and is sentenced to death by firing squad. He is later assassinated in 1983.
Sangoulé Lamizana, president of Upper Volta, is ousted from power in a coup d'état led by Colonel Saye Zerbo.

main.desc: President of Upper Volta from 1966 to 1980

events.text: A group of Conservative members of Parliament wrote a letter outlining their opposition to the economic policy of Margaret Thatcher, leading to speculation over a split from the party.

main.desc: Group of British Conservative Party backbench MPs

events.text: Pope John Paul II appoints Joseph Cardinal Ratzinger (the future Pope Benedict XVI) Prefect of the Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1978 to 2005

links.t: Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith

events.text: Band Aid, a supergroup consisting of more than 30 leading British and Irish pop musicians, recorded the song "Do They Know It's Christmas?" to raise money for famine relief in Ethiopia.
Thirty-six top musicians gather in a Notting Hill studio and record Band Aid's "Do They Know It's Christmas?" in order to raise money for famine relief in Ethiopia.
A Soviet Air Force Antonov An-12 is shot down near Menongue in Angola's Cuando Cubango Province, killing 21.

main.desc: Aerial warfare branch of the Soviet Union's armed forces

events.text: Iran–Contra affair: U.S. Attorney General Edwin Meese announces that profits from covert weapons sales to Iran were illegally diverted to the anti-communist Contra rebels in Nicaragua.
The King Fahd Causeway is officially opened in the Persian Gulf.

main.desc: Road connection between Khobar, Saudi Arabia and Bahrain

events.text: Typhoon Nina pummels the Philippines with category 5 winds of 265 km/h (165 mph) and a surge that destroys entire villages. At least 1,036 deaths are attributed to the storm.
The Federal Assembly of Czechoslovakia votes to split the country into the Czech Republic and Slovakia, with effect from January 1, 1993.

main.desc: Legislature of Czechoslovakia from 1969 to its dissolution in 1992

events.text: A five-year-old Cuban boy, Elián González, is rescued by fishermen while floating in an inner tube off the Florida coast.

main.desc: Cuban boy in 2000 international custody dispute

events.text: The 2000 Baku earthquake, with a Richter magnitude of 7.0 kills 26 people dead in Baku, Azerbaijan, being the strongest earthquake in the region in 158 years.
Cyclone Nisha strikes northern Sri Lanka, killing 15 people and displacing 90,000 others while dealing the region the highest rainfall in nine decades.

main.desc: Tropical cyclone in the Indian Ocean

events.text: Jeddah floods: Freak rains swamp the city of Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, during an ongoing Hajj pilgrimage. Three thousand cars are swept away and 122 people perish in the torrents, with 350 others missing.

main.desc: 2009 natural disaster in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia

events.text: English-Irish boy band One Direction released their third studio album Midnight Memories which debuted at number one on the Billboard 200 and became the best-selling album of 2013.
The Asturian queen Adosinda is held at a monastery to prevent her nephew from retaking the throne from Mauregatus.

main.desc: Kingdom in the Northern Iberian Peninsula (718–924)

events.text: Battle of Caishi: A Song dynasty fleet fights a naval engagement with Jin dynasty ships on the Yangtze river during the Jin–Song Wars.
Having been elected German king at Rhens on 11 July 1346, Charles IV is crowned King of Germany by bishop Walram of Cologne in Bonn.
Vlad the Impaler defeats Basarab Laiota with the help of Stephen the Great and Stephen V Báthory and becomes the ruler of Wallachia for the third time.
In the Hawaiian Islands, Captain James Cook becomes the first European to visit Maui.
A national Thanksgiving Day is observed in the United States as proclaimed by President George Washington at the request of Congress.
Official opening of Thomas Telford's Pontcysyllte Aqueduct.
The Battle of Berezina begins during Napoleon's retreat from Russia.

main.desc: 1812 battle during the French invasion of Russia

events.text: Texas Revolution: Texian forces attacked a Mexican pack train, capturing 40 saddlebags of grass.
The University of Notre Dame (building pictured) was founded by Edward Sorin of the Congregation of Holy Cross as an all-male institution in the U.S. state of Indiana.

main.desc: Catholic university in Notre Dame, Indiana, U.S.

events.text: The French navy bombarded Salé, Morocco (pictured), damaging the city's infrastructure and its Great Mosque.

main.desc: Topics referred to by the same term

events.text: A massive earthquake struck the Dutch East Indies, creating a tsunami that washed away villages, ships and residents.
An earthquake as high as magnitude 8.8 rocks the Banda Sea, triggering a tsunami and killing at least 60 in the Dutch East Indies.

United States President Abraham Lincoln proclaims November 26 as a national Thanksgiving Day, to be celebrated annually on the final Thursday of November.  Following the Franksgiving controversy from 1939 to 1941, it has been observed on the fourth Thursday in 1942 and subsequent years.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1861 to 1865

events.text: Battle of Papudo: A Spanish navy schooner is defeated by a Chilean corvette north of Valparaíso, Chile.

main.desc: 1865 naval battle of the Chincha Islands War

events.text: A large internal explosion destroyed HMS Bulwark near Sheerness, killing 741 people on board.

main.desc: Pre-dreadnought battleship of the British Royal Navy

events.text: HMS Bulwark is destroyed by a large internal explosion with the loss of 741 men while at anchor near Sheerness.

main.desc: Pre-dreadnought battleship of the British Royal Navy

events.text: Being unable to resolve disputes with Eddie Livingstone, owner of the Toronto Blueshirts, the other ice hockey clubs of Canada's National Hockey Association officially agreed to break away and form the National Hockey League.
The Manchester Guardian publishes the 1916 secret Sykes-Picot Agreement between the United Kingdom and France.
The National Hockey League is formed, with the Montreal Canadiens, Montreal Wanderers, Ottawa Senators, Quebec Bulldogs, and Toronto Arenas as its first teams.

main.desc: North American professional ice hockey league

events.text: The Montenegrin Podgorica Assembly votes for a "union of the people", declaring assimilation into the Kingdom of Serbia.
Ukrainian War of Independence: The Red Army launches a surprise attack against the Makhnovshchina.
The Bolshevik–Makhnovist conflict resumes with a surprise attack by the Red Army against the Makhnovshchina.

main.desc: 1920–21 political and military conflict in southern Ukraine

events.text: Howard Carter and Lord Carnarvon become the first people to enter the tomb of Pharaoh Tutankhamun in over 3,000 years.
The Toll of the Sea debuts as the first general release film to use two-tone Technicolor. (The Gulf Between was the first film to do so, but it was not widely distributed.)
The Mongolian People's Republic is officially established after a new constitution, passed by the first State Great Khural, abolishes the monarchy.

links.t: Constitutions of the Mongolian People's Republic

events.text: The Soviet Red Army shelled the village of Mainila and then claimed that the fire originated from Finland, giving them a casus belli to launch the Winter War a few days later.

main.desc: Soviet army and air force from 1918 to 1946

events.text: Shelling of Mainila: The Soviet Army orchestrates an incident which is used to justify the start of the Winter War with Finland four days later.

main.desc: 1939 false flag attack by the Soviet Union against Finland, leading to the Winter War

events.text: The Iron Guard killed 64 political detainees at a penitentiary near Bucharest and followed up with several high-profile assassinations, including that of former Romanian prime minister Nicolae Iorga.

main.desc: Romanian fascist movement and political party

events.text: World War II: The Hull note is given to the Japanese ambassador, demanding that Japan withdraw from China and French Indochina, in return for which the United States would lift economic sanctions. On the same day, Japan's 1st Air Fleet departs Hitokappu Bay for Hawaii.
Casablanca, starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, premiered at the Hollywood Theatre in New York City to coincide with the Allied invasion of French North Africa and the capture of Casablanca.
World War II: Josip Broz Tito and the Yugoslav Partisans convened the first meeting of the Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia at Bihać in northwestern Bosnia.

links.t: Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia

events.text: A riot involving infantrymen, military police, and local law enforcement officers killed three people in Phoenix, Arizona.
World War II: Yugoslav Partisans convene the first meeting of the Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia at Bihać in northwestern Bosnia.

main.desc: Communist-led anti-Axis resistance in World War II

links.t: Anti-Fascist Council for the National Liberation of Yugoslavia

events.text: Casablanca, the movie starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, premieres in New York City.
A riot involving infantrymen, military police, and local law enforcement officers occurs in Phoenix, Arizona, United States, leading to three deaths.
World War II: HMT Rohna is sunk by the Luftwaffe in an air attack in the Mediterranean north of Béjaïa, Algeria.

main.desc: British passenger and cargo liner; sunk in 1943 by Nazi air forces

events.text: World War II: A German V-2 rocket hits a Woolworth's shop in New Cross, London, killing 168 people.
World War II: Germany begins V-1 and V-2 attacks on Antwerp, Belgium.
The Constituent Assembly of India adopts the constitution presented by Dr. B. R. Ambedkar.

main.desc: Unicameral assembly for making the Constitution of India

events.text: Korean War: Communist Chinese troops launch a massive counterattack (Battle of the Ch'ongch'on River and Battle of Chosin Reservoir) against United Nations and South Korean forces.
France launches Astérix, becoming the third nation to put an object in orbit using its own booster.
Vietnam War: United States Air Force helicopter pilot James P. Fleming rescues an Army Special Forces unit pinned down by Viet Cong fire. He is later awarded the Medal of Honor.
In Basse-Terre, Guadeloupe, 38 millimetres (1.5 in) of rain fall in a minute, the heaviest rainfall ever recorded.
A speaker claiming to represent the "Intergalactic Association" interrupted a broadcast of Southern Television in South East England.

main.desc: TV audio transmission hoax in southern England (1977)

events.text: An unidentified hijacker named Vrillon, claiming to be the representative of the "Ashtar Galactic Command", takes over Britain's Southern Television for six minutes, starting at 5:12 pm.

main.desc: TV audio transmission hoax in southern England (1977)

events.text: Pakistan International Airlines Flight 740, crashed shortly after takeoff near Taif, Saudi Arabia, killing all 156 people on board.
Pakistan International Airlines Flight 740 crashes near Taif in Mecca Province, Saudi Arabia, killing all 156 people on board.
Six robbers broke into a Brink's-Mat warehouse at Heathrow Airport in London and stole £26 million in gold, diamonds and cash.
Brink's-Mat robbery: In London, 6,800 gold bars worth nearly £26 million are stolen from the Brink's-Mat vault at Heathrow Airport.
Iran–Contra affair: U.S. President Ronald Reagan announces the members of what will become known as the Tower Commission.
The trial of John Demjanjuk, accused of committing war crimes as a guard at the Nazi Treblinka extermination camp, starts in Jerusalem.

main.desc: Ukrainian guard at Nazi death camps (1920–2012)

events.text: National Assembly of Azerbaijan abolishes the autonomous status of Nagorno-Karabakh Autonomous Oblast of Azerbaijan and renames several cities with Azeri names.

events.text: U.S. Secretary of Defense Robert McNamara announces his resignation.

main.desc: Head of the US Department of Defense

events.text: Atari announced the release of Pong (screenshot pictured), one of the first video games to achieve widespread popularity in both the arcade and home-console markets.
Atari releases Pong, the first commercially successful video game.

The controversial Tellico Dam project by the Tennessee Valley Authority is completed despite being ordered to shut down from the Supreme Court of the United States' decision in Tennessee Valley Authority v. Hill.

links.t: Supreme Court of the United States

events.text: Michael Jackson's Thriller, the best-selling album of all time, was released.
Michael Jackson releases Thriller, the best-selling music album of all time.
The Surinamese military attacks the village of Moiwana during the Suriname Guerrilla War, killing at least 39 civilians, mostly women and children.
A time bomb planted by North Korean agents on Korean Air Flight 858 detonated over the Andaman Sea, killing all 115 people on board.

main.desc: Explosive device whose detonation is triggered by a timer

events.text: North Korean agents plant a bomb on Korean Air Flight 858, which kills all 115 passengers and crew.

main.desc: 1987 aircraft bombing over the Andaman Sea

events.text: During their trial for the 2003 Oakwood mutiny, Philippine soldiers led by Senator Antonio Trillanes mutinied and seized a conference room at The Peninsula Manila in Makati.
The Armed Forces of the Philippines lay siege to the Peninsula Manila after soldiers led by Senator Antonio Trillanes stage a mutiny.
Maurice Clemmons shoots and kills four police officers inside a coffee shop in Lakewood, Washington.
In resolution 67/19, the United Nations General Assembly voted to accord the status of a non-member observer state to Palestine.
LAM Mozambique Airlines 470 crashes in the Bwabata National Park in a pilot mass murder-suicide, killing all 33 people on board.
The Government of Jordan officially announces the launch of the Amra City development project during a site visit by the Prime Minister.
Abu al Abbas celebrates a victory parade in Bagdhad following the suppression of the Zanj Rebellion, the largest slave revolt in the Arab world.
Franco-German war of 978–980: Holy Roman Emperor Otto II lifts the siege of Paris and withdraws.

main.desc: West Francia vs. Holy Roman Empire

events.text: Great Northern War: Swedish forces led by King Charles XII defeated the Russian army at the Battle of Narva.
Queen Anne's War: The second Siege of Pensacola comes to end with the failure of the British Empire and their Creek allies to capture Pensacola, Spanish Florida.

main.desc: North American theater of the War of the Spanish Succession (1702–1713)

events.text: Great Northern War: King Charles XII of Sweden dies during a siege of the fortress of Fredriksten in Norway.
American Revolutionary War: Treaty of Paris: In Paris, representatives from the United States and Great Britain sign preliminary peace articles (later formalized as the 1783 Treaty of Paris).
The Grand Duchy of Tuscany, under Pietro Leopoldo I, becomes the first modern state to abolish the death penalty (later commemorated as Cities for Life Day).
An expedition led by Francisco Javier de Balmis departed A Coruña, Spain, with the aim of vaccinating millions in South America and Asia against smallpox.
The Balmis Expedition starts in Spain with the aim of vaccinating millions against smallpox in Spanish America and Philippines.
In New Orleans, Spanish representatives officially transfer the Louisiana Territory to the French First Republic.

main.desc: Territory of the United States of America from 1805 to 1812

events.text: Russian warships led by Pavel Nakhimov destroyed an Ottoman fleet of frigates at the Battle of Sinop, prompting France and the United Kingdom to enter the Crimean War.
Crimean War: Battle of Sinop: The Imperial Russian Navy under Pavel Nakhimov destroys the Ottoman fleet under Osman Pasha at Sinop, a sea port in northern Turkey.

main.desc: Tenth conflict of the Russo-Turkish wars (1853–1856)

events.text: American Civil War: The Confederate Army of Tennessee led by General John Bell Hood suffers heavy losses in an attack on the Union Army of the Ohio under General John Schofield in the Battle of Franklin.
The first international football match (pictured) took place at Hamilton Crescent, Glasgow, between Scotland and England.
The first-ever international football match takes place at Hamilton Crescent, Glasgow, between Scotland and England.
Costa Rica signs the Buenos Aires Convention, a copyright treaty.
Flying Scotsman (pictured) became the first steam locomotive officially to exceed 100 miles per hour (161 km/h).
A college football game between the SMU Mustangs and the TCU Horned Frogs became the first game in Texas to be broadcast nationally on radio.
English mathematician Alan Turing published the first details of the Turing machine (model pictured), an abstract device that can simulate the logic of any computer algorithm by manipulating symbols.
In London, the Crystal Palace is destroyed by fire.

main.desc: Glasshouse for the 1851 Great Exhibition in London

events.text: World War II: The Soviet Red Army crosses the Finnish border in several places, bombing Helsinki and several other Finnish cities, starting the Winter War.

links.t: Bombing of Helsinki in World War II

events.text: World War II: Signing of the Sino-Japanese Treaty of 1940 between the Empire of Japan and the newly formed Wang Jingwei-led Reorganized National Government of the Republic of China. This treaty was considered so unfair to China that it was compared to the Twenty-One Demands.
The Holocaust: The SS-Einsatzgruppen round up roughly 25,000 Jews from the Riga Ghetto and kill them in the Rumbula massacre.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: World War II: Japanese warships defeated the U.S. Navy in a nighttime naval battle off Tassafaronga, Guadalcanal.
World War II: Battle of Tassafaronga; A smaller squadron of Imperial Japanese Navy destroyers led by Raizō Tanaka defeats a U.S. Navy cruiser force under Carleton H. Wright.

main.desc: 1942 naval battle in the Pacific theater of World War II

events.text: After the United Nations voted to adopt a partition plan for Palestine, a civil war broke out between the region's Jewish and Arab communities.

main.t: United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine

events.text: Civil War in Mandatory Palestine begins, leading up to the creation of the State of Israel and the 1948 Arab–Israeli War.

main.desc: First phase of the 1947–1949 Palestine war

events.text: Mutesa II, Kabaka of Buganda, was temporarily deposed and exiled to London by Andrew Cohen, the British governor of Uganda.

main.desc: Monarch of the Kingdom of Buganda from 1939 to 1969

events.text: Edward Mutesa II, the kabaka (king) of Buganda is deposed and exiled to London by Sir Andrew Cohen, Governor of Uganda.

main.desc: Monarch of the Kingdom of Buganda from 1939 to 1969

events.text: A meteorite crashed through a roof in Sylacauga, Alabama, and hit a sleeping woman in the first verified case of a human being injured by an extraterrestrial object.

main.desc: Meteorite that fell in 1954 in Alabama

events.text: In Sylacauga, Alabama, United States, the Hodges meteorite crashes through a roof and hits a woman taking an afternoon nap; this is the only documented case in the Western Hemisphere of a human being hit by a rock from space.
President Sukarno of Indonesia escapes a grenade attack that kills multiple bystanders.
Eastern Air Lines Flight 512 crashes at Idlewild Airport, killing 25 people.
Decolonization: Barbados becomes independent from the United Kingdom.

main.desc: Undoing political, economic and cultural legacies of colonisation

events.text: The People's Republic of Southern Yemen gains its independence from the United Kingdom
The Pakistan Peoples Party is founded by Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, who becomes its first chairman.
Pro-Soviet communists in the Philippines establish Malayang Pagkakaisa ng Kabataan Pilipino as its new youth wing.
Iran seizes the Greater and Lesser Tunbs from the Emirates of Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah.

links.t: Seizure of Abu Musa and the Greater and Lesser Tunbs

events.text: Vietnam War: White House Press Secretary Ron Ziegler tells the press that there will be no more public announcements concerning American troop withdrawals from Vietnam because troop levels are now down to 27,000.
The Wall, a rock opera and concept album by the English band Pink Floyd, was first released.

Cold War: In Geneva, representatives from the United States and the Soviet Union begin to negotiate intermediate-range nuclear weapon reductions in Europe. (The meetings end inconclusively on December 17.)

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: Official end of Operation Desert Storm.
U.S. President Bill Clinton visits Northern Ireland and speaks in favor of the "Northern Ireland peace process" to a huge rally at Belfast City Hall; he calls IRA fighters "yesterday's men".

main.desc: President of the United States from 1993 to 2001

events.text: A series of protests by anti-globalization activists against the World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 1999 in Seattle forced the cancellation of the opening ceremonies.

links.t: World Trade Organization Ministerial Conference of 1999

events.text: Exxon and Mobil sign a US$73.7 billion agreement to merge, thus creating ExxonMobil, the world's largest company.

main.desc: American multinational oil and gas company

events.text: In Seattle, United States, demonstrations against a World Trade Organization meeting by anti-globalization protesters catch police unprepared and force the cancellation of opening ceremonies.
British Aerospace and Marconi Electronic Systems merge to form BAE Systems, Europe's largest defense contractor and the fourth largest aerospace firm in the world.
NASA launches STS-97, the 101st Space Shuttle mission.

main.desc: 2000 American crewed spaceflight to the ISS

events.text: A McDonnell Douglas MD-82, operating as Lion Air Flight 538, overran the runway at Adisoemarmo Airport and crashed, killing 25 people.

main.desc: Jet airliner model, series based on the DC-9

events.text: John Sentamu was enthroned as Archbishop of York, becoming the first black archbishop in the Church of England.
John Sentamu becomes the first black archbishop in the Church of England with his enthronement as the 97th Archbishop of York.
Atlasjet Flight 4203 crashes in Keçiborlu while on approach to Isparta Süleyman Demirel Airport, killing 57.
A magnitude-7.1 earthquake (aftermath pictured) hit Anchorage, Alaska, causing 117 injuries.
A magnitude 7.1 earthquake with its epicenter only 24 km from Anchorage, Alaska causes significant property damage but no deaths.
Barbados becomes a republic.

main.desc: Island nation in the Atlantic Ocean

events.text: A 15-year-old gunman murders four students and injures seven people, including a teacher, in a mass shooting at Oxford High School in Oxford Township, Michigan.
The generative AI chatbot ChatGPT is launched by OpenAI.
